items.title: Christian McBride interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: So I joined Freddie’s band and I stayed in his band for about two and a half or three years

ctx.x: That’s a great attitude I think. Who were some of the horn players that caught your ear when you got into jazz?

Freddie Hubbard. Freddie Hubbard was probably my biggest non-bass influence as far as writing, as far as improvising. I first heard Freddie’s CTI Records like “Red Clay” and all that stuff, and I heard the records he made with Art Blakey and I heard his Blue Note records. And then when I saw him in person I’ll never forget, I almost passed out because I’d never seen anyone play with that much — that was my first time actually witnessing a jazz musician with that much fire playing in person. And I remember I…
You got your education right there.
